text.p: - Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek said salary growth ought to slow. Wages should grow more slowly than GDP in order to increase industry competitiveness, he said.
- Jacques Santer, president of the European Commission will visit Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek and president Milan Kucan on Friday.
- Five people died in traffic accidents on Wednesday in the Ljubljana area.

- Slovenian Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler visited representatives of Slovenian industry in Hungary on Wednesday, he said building a railway connection between the two countries was among the primary tasks of the two neighbouring countries.
- Ministry of Economic Relations and Development said the validity of privatisation vouchers would not be extended beyond the current expiry date June 30.
- Domestic savings and direct foreign investment should be stimulated as much as possible, Jozko Cuk, president of Slovenian Economic Chamber said.
- The central bank governor France Arhar said there were no plans to abolish rules that force international portfolio investors to open custody accounts in order to trade in Slovenian securities.
- Slovenian GSM consortium said it would invest up to 120 million marks in next five years in developing a mobile phone network, if its bid for Slovenia's second licence succeeded.
- Tour de Slovenia, the biggest Slovenian bicycle race will be cancelled this year due to financial problems affecting the organizers, the country's cycling federation said.
- Reconstruction of Ljubljana's airport Brnik which started in 1988 cost 60 million marks.
- Slovenian president Milan Kucan met representatives of Slovenian minority living in Austria on Wednesday.
